attacks.claim: The unpublish control is an icon-only <span> with only an onClick. It has no button role, no tabIndex, no keyboard handler, and no accessible name (the icon is aria-hidden). Keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot reach, activate, or identify a destructive action, which violates the WCAG 2.1 AA release requirement.

The embargo badge text is hard-coded #ffffff on background var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The text is invisible, so the badge's core information is unreadable by default and fails WCAG 1.4.3 contrast.
attacks.evidence: background: var(--surface); color: #ffffff;  with --surface: #ffffff in :root (light is default)

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch, pending state, or in-flight guard. A failed unpublish of a live story gives no feedback and produces an unhandled rejection. Repeated clicks can stack confirm dialogs or fire duplicate requests.
attacks.evidence: if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);  (no error handling, no disabled or pending state)

attacks.claim: The unpublish control has a :hover style but no :focus-visible style. Once it is made focusable, keyboard focus would have no visible indicator.

The diff shows no role gate on the unpublish control and no audit record of who unpublished a story. Authorization and audit logging would live in the onUnpublish/server path, which is not in this diff, so this cannot be verified from the PR. Worth confirming.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: role check or audit logging in the shown change; only a client-side confirm dialog

attacks.claim: The badge shows a lift time in the newsroom timezone but does not label the timezone, so editors in other zones may misread it.
A trash icon implies deletion, but the action unpublishes the story and returns it to drafts. The mismatch could mislead editors.
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> with confirm copy "returned to drafts"

attacks.claim: The embargo state is computed from client-side new Date() at render with no timer, so a lifted embargo keeps showing until an unrelated re-render. The !== null guard and the non-null assertion are also fragile.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();
